screening_decisions.reason: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot RCT of intracervical nitroprusside gel before IUD placement; primary outcome was self-reported pain with insertion.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of ibuprofen 800 mg versus placebo 30–45 minutes prior to IUD insertion; patient-reported pain with insertion measured (VAS).
Randomized trial of bladder filling strategy (delayed vs immediate emptying) to reduce insertion-related pain; women’s pain scores during IUD insertion were measured.
Randomized clinical trial comparing intracervical 2% lidocaine injection vs pre-insertion oral NSAID; patient-reported pain immediately after insertion and at 2h/6h recorded.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of ibuprofen 800 mg vs placebo 45 minutes prior to LNG-IUS insertion; pain at tenaculum and during insertion assessed.
Double-blind, multicenter RCT of vaginal misoprostol vs placebo 3h prior to IUD insertion; insertion-related pain outcomes reported.
Randomized, placebo-controlled RCT in nulliparous women of buccal misoprostol vs placebo; self-reported pain at tenaculum and during insertion measured (VAS).
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of sublingual misoprostol vs placebo for consecutive LNG-IUS replacement; pain at insertion recorded.
Large randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of prophylactic ibuprofen 400 mg vs placebo before IUD insertion; immediate post-insertion pain VAS outcome.
Single-blind RCT in parous women with prior elective cesarean only; sublingual misoprostol+diclofenac vs diclofenac; insertion-related pain and complications assessed.
Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study of ibuprofen peri-insertion (pre and post); pain during insertion and up to 6 hours after assessed via numerical scales.
Randomized, double-blind clinical trial comparing oral tramadol, naproxen sodium, and placebo 1 hour prior to insertion; insertion pain VAS primary outcome.
Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of buccal misoprostol vs placebo in nulliparous women; provider ease and patient-reported pain during insertion measured.
Randomized, double-blind clinical trial of intracervical 2% lidocaine gel vs placebo; pain at sounding and during IUD insertion assessed with VAS.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot RCT of vaginal nitroglycerin gel vs placebo 30 minutes prior to LNG-IUS insertion; procedural pain outcomes measured.
Randomized trial of 1% lidocaine paracervical block vs no anesthetic; self-reported pain at tenaculum placement, insertion, and 5 minutes postprocedure recorded.
Randomized controlled trial with three arms (2% lidocaine gel, lubricant gel, no intervention) evaluating VAS pain during copper IUD insertion.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot of intrauterine lidocaine vs saline infusion prior to IUD insertion; pain at tenaculum and during insertion recorded.
Randomized controlled trial in nulliparous women of sublingual misoprostol+diclofenac vs diclofenac; pain during insertion measured via VAS.
Randomized, double-blind clinical trial of vaginal misoprostol 4h before insertion vs placebo; reported reduction in moderate-to-severe insertion pain.
Randomized trial of inhaled lavender aromatherapy vs placebo 30 minutes before insertion; anxiety and insertion pain (VAS) measured.
Randomized, placebo-controlled RCT of self-administered misoprostol (vaginal/buccal) vs placebo 3–4 hours before insertion; pain before/immediately after insertion assessed.
Randomized, placebo-controlled phase II trial of a novel topical lidocaine formulation applied to portio/cervix/uterus; significant reduction in maximum pain within 10 minutes post-insertion.

Prospective, single-blinded, controlled study with paracervical lidocaine vs placebo vs no treatment; pain at tenaculum, insertion, and 5 minutes post measured. Randomization not explicit—include with caution.
Randomized clinical trial of misoprostol vs placebo before insertion in nulliparous women; primary outcome was insertion pain (100-mm VAS).

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (abstract) of self-administered 2% lidocaine gel vs placebo 5 minutes prior to insertion; pain at multiple time points including tenaculum and insertion.
Not an RCT; descriptive practice report of intracervical anesthesia technique without randomized comparison.
Not an RCT; prospective cohort comparing pain by parity history, not evaluating a preventive intervention.
Not an RCT; qualitative study on perceptions/acceptability, not an intervention trial for insertion pain.
Not an RCT; narrative/practical review without randomized evaluation of interventions.

Not an RCT; committee opinion on LARC use, not an intervention trial on IUD insertion pain.

Not an RCT; review of misoprostol in gynecology across procedures, not specific RCT for IUD insertion pain prevention.
Not an RCT; observational evaluation of expected vs actual pain during insertion.

Randomized clinical trial with three groups (lavender aromatherapy, sesame oil placebo, control) evaluating pain during IUD insertion (VAS).

Not an RCT; Cochrane review of NSAIDs for bleeding or pain associated with IUD use (includes prophylaxis but is not a primary RCT).
